version.changelog:
- Added new metadata file: _meta.json.
- No changes to user-facing features or skill behavior.

llm.summary: The skill itself is a simple daily book recommendation, but its install notes tell users to run an unspecified publisher-provided installer outside the reviewed package.

dimensions.detail: The documented default setup creates a daily OpenClaw cron push to Telegram/Slack; this persistence and external posting are disclosed and aligned with a daily-book skill, but users should confirm the destination and schedule.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: INSTALL.md includes a normal reviewed install command, but also instructs users to directly copy and execute a future publisher-provided one-command installer that is not included, pinned, checksummed, or inspectable in this artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are narrow and formatting-focused, though examples and the scheduled default message are Chinese-oriented despite English triggers and a user-language claim.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The reviewed cron command is explicit, but the separate unreviewed installer is described as automatically completing installation and writing configuration, creating unclear mutation authority outside the reviewed package.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill's runtime purpose is coherent: fetch one book from a configured/default API and generate a short optimistic reading in the user's language.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Prefer the reviewed `clawhub install book-of-the-day` path and manually review any cron/channel settings before enabling daily pushes. Do not run a separate publisher-supplied one-command installer unless its full contents, source, version, and checksum/signature are available and trusted.
llm.findings:
[SQP-3] unexpected: The Chinese-only install guide and fixed Chinese scheduled message are a localization and disclosure concern, but the skill metadata also includes English triggers and says to respond in the user's language; this did not drive the security verdict by itself.
[T08] unexpected: The artifact confirms INSTALL.md tells users to directly execute a publisher-provided one-command installer that is not present for review; this is a real supply-chain and install-scope concern, though not evidence of malicious behavior.
